analysis.title: The Day Ahead for Wednesday, October 28, 2026
key_insights: AI-fueled tech rally lifted US stocks on Oct 27: S&P 500 +0.60% to 7,722.66, Nasdaq +1.18% to 26,477.81, DJIA +0.03% to 52,378.40. A strategist quoted in the note attributed the chip rebound to the Anthropic news after recent heavy selling in semis.
Nearly half of S&P 500 companies have reported Q3 results, and 83% beat expectations per the most recent available LSEG data.

The Fed decision is due Wednesday at 14:00 ET, with the funds rate expected unchanged at 3.75%-4%. Chair Kevin Warsh holds a news conference afterward. The note calls it the Fed's penultimate meeting of the year.

Treasury yields edged higher in narrow ranges ahead of the Fed. The 10-year yields about 4.99-5.00% and the 30-year 5.31%. Yields fell last week as AI-boom sustainability fears sparked an equity selloff and a bid for bonds. Jefferies' Simons says inflation risks are higher than the market expects.
The Treasury sold $70B of 5-year notes at a high yield of 4.845% with a bid-to-cover of 2.33.

The dollar index rose 0.34% to 102.30, with EUR/USD down about 0.35% to 1.1133 and USD/JPY at 157.92. Convera's Ford said markets have taken some pressure off the Fed to hike, after last week's equity distress, high oil prices and French fiscal stress.

Oil fell on Middle East peace-talk headlines: Brent -1.67% to $113.88 and WTI -1.9% to $99.83. Analysts cite continued Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and the Gulf military buildup as keeping supply risk in place.
Spot gold rose about 1.1% to roughly $4,060 as lower oil eased inflation worries and moderated expectations of Fed hawkishness.
Alphabet and Microsoft report after the close Wednesday. The focus is AI spending, cloud growth and capex commentary. Amazon is also expected to report accelerating cloud growth this week.

Rising bond yields at AI cloud providers such as CoreWeave and record costs to insure Meta's debt have raised concerns about how the AI buildout is funded. Ken Griffin has warned of an AI bubble, and some companies have delayed IPOs.

Boeing fell 10.9% to $167.78 after CEO Ortberg said the company will miss its 2026 737 production and delivery targets. Free cash flow is now expected to reach $10B in 2029, a year later than consensus.

Coca-Cola raised its annual profit forecast on international demand (India, Brazil) but flagged accelerating cost pressures and consumer weakness into 2027. Consumer goods companies are warning of further price hikes as the Iran war lifts commodity costs.
JetBlue rose 18.99% to $2.82 after it raised its revenue forecast and rejected restructuring talk following a bond sell-off. Short interest is 25%. The company reiterated a $1 EPS target for 2028.

PayPal raised its annual profit forecast on cost cuts and margin expansion. UPS raised its annual revenue and profit forecasts and expects Q4 average daily volume -1.3%, domestic revenue about +3% and international revenue about +7%.
Hilton missed Q3 revenue estimates and warned that the Middle East conflict and the US midterms could weigh on Q4. Middle East and Africa room revenue fell 5.6% y/y and US room revenue rose 7%.

Core capital goods orders ex-aircraft rose 0.5% in September after an unrevised +1.6% in August. Core shipments rose 1.2%, and +8.8% y/y. Conference Board consumer confidence rose 7.5 points to 91.7. New home sales fell 0.6% to 676K annualized.

Nvidia is investing $3B in Meta's equity offering. Argentum AI is in talks for $5B AI chip financing with a private credit firm. Moody's says AI financing is driving private credit growth while refinancing risk rises.
Bank of Canada is expected to raise its policy rate to 2.5% from 2.25% on Wednesday. A pending increase in US tariffs on Canadian steel and autos from Jan 1 is being flagged by automakers.

Other items: NYSE is preparing all-or-nothing options on stocks and ETFs, the CFTC-type regulator is again probing Polymarket, GM is moving its listing to Nasdaq, and crypto industry groups have spent about $176M on midterm races.

market_movers.rationale: Boeing fell 10.9% to $167.78 after it said it will miss 2026 737 production and delivery targets. It now expects to reach its $10B free cash flow target in 2029, a year later than consensus.
JetBlue rose 18.99% to $2.82 after it raised its revenue forecast and denied restructuring talks. Short interest is 25%.
Coca-Cola raised its annual profit forecast on international soda demand but warned of accelerating costs and consumer weakness into 2027.
PayPal raised its annual profit forecast on cost cuts and margin expansion under CEO Lores.
UPS raised annual revenue and profit forecasts after cutting unprofitable Amazon volume. It expects Q4 average daily volume -1.3%.
Hilton missed Q3 revenue estimates and warned of Middle East and midterm-election effects on Q4.
Dell rose 7.6% to $502.59 in the AI-led tech rally.
Xylem fell 12.77% to $94.42 on Oct 27. The note gives no reason.
Valero fell 8.79% to $389.26 on Oct 27, as oil dropped. The note gives no reason.

earnings_insights: Alphabet Q3 reports after close 10/28: LSEG EPS estimate $3.02 (Smart Estimate $3.03), revenue estimate $128,222M, year-ago EPS $3.10. These are estimates, not results.
Microsoft fiscal Q1 2027 reports after close 10/28: EPS estimate $4.72 (Smart Estimate $4.74), revenue estimate $90,663M, year-ago EPS $4.13. Estimates only.
Ford Q3 reports after close 10/28: EPS estimate $0.40 (Smart Estimate $0.41), revenue estimate $46,238M, year-ago EPS $0.45. Focus is raw material costs and production disruptions.

GE Vernova Q3 reports before the open 10/28: EPS estimate $3.97 (Smart Estimate $3.95) vs year-ago $1.67, revenue estimate $11,991M. Gas turbine and grid demand is expected to drive results, and the wind business is the main concern.

Phillips 66 Q3 reports before the open 10/28: EPS estimate $11.73 (Smart Estimate $12.10) vs year-ago $2.52. Stronger refining margins are expected to lift earnings. HF Sinclair is also expected to report higher adjusted earnings.

Other 10/28 reports with LSEG EPS estimates: ServiceNow $1.02, KLA $1.18, Fortinet $0.86, T-Mobile $2.91, eBay $1.41, Carvana $0.44, Chipotle $0.29, Biogen $1.97, Boeing is not listed. FedEx lists no estimates.
Reported on 10/27, per the note: Coca-Cola, PayPal and UPS raised annual profit forecasts. JetBlue raised its revenue forecast. Hilton missed Q3 revenue estimates.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Poll expects no change at the Wednesday 14:00 ET decision. Markets are focused on Chair Warsh's press conference for guidance on possible hikes.
Poll for the 08:30 ET release. Prior was -$132.07B.
Prior reading, no poll shown for September.
Follows an unrevised +1.6% in August, consistent with firm AI-related business equipment spending.
These feed the equipment spending component of GDP, pointing to a solid Q3.
Up 7.5 points, attributed to easing gasoline prices.

crypto_views: The crypto industry has spent about $176M across 100+ midterm races to build a bipartisan coalition in Congress for the post-Trump era. The industry is described as worth $2.75T.
The CFTC-style US regulator, unnamed in the note, is again investigating whether Polymarket violated a 2022 settlement over banning US users.
risk_factors: AI buildout financing: rising bond yields at AI cloud providers such as CoreWeave, record costs to insure Meta's debt, and refinancing risk in AI-linked private credit per Moody's.
Higher US rates ahead: the note says the Fed is expected to hike rather than ease and Jefferies sees inflation risks as more pronounced than the market expects.
Oil-driven inflation: Brent above $113 and war-related cost pressure on consumer goods makers.
Middle East escalation and Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia.
French fiscal stress and equity-market distress hit the dollar last week.
US midterm election outcomes may affect data centers and AI infrastructure.
US tariffs on Canadian steel and autos from January 1.
vol_and_positioning: A Reuters Open Interest column by Mike Dolan says October's AI-sector turbulence suggests the AI boom's shield against market fears is cracking. It expects more discrimination within the sector and notes that disturbances can spread across broad indexes and other asset classes.
Last week's AI-driven equity selloff pushed investors into bonds. Semis that were 'clobbered' in recent weeks bounced on Oct 27.
JetBlue short interest is 25% of the float.
NYSE is preparing all-or-nothing (binary) options on stocks and ETFs that settle on whether the close is above or below a set price.
geopolitical: Middle East peace talks: Iranian Security Council chief Mohsen Rezaei met Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei a day after talks with Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan, who agreed to continue talks on peace and security cooperation.
Continued Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and an expanding military presence in the Gulf keep oil supply risks in place.
The US war with Iran is raising commodity, packaging and freight costs, according to the Coca-Cola item, and Hilton cited an escalation in the US-Iran war.
US tariff increase on Canadian steel and autos scheduled for January 1, with US-Mexico-Canada trade deal talks under way.
European fiscal stress coming from France was cited by Convera as a factor in last week's dollar moves.
US midterm elections: an expected Democratic sweep could add pressure on data centers, which already face protests over power grids and electricity bills.
Canada and the UAE signed a comprehensive economic partnership agreement.

tension_points.bull_case: Cloud growth is expected to accelerate at Amazon, Microsoft and Alphabet. Capital goods orders and shipments show AI-related equipment spending holding up, and chip stocks rebounded.
tension_points.bear_case: Rising bond yields at AI cloud providers, record Meta debt insurance costs, bubble warnings from Ken Griffin, delayed IPOs and Moody's refinancing risk warnings for AI-linked private credit.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Big Tech earnings that fail to show swift returns on AI spending, per the investor demands described in the note.

theme_stances.key_argument: Last week's turbulence shows investors preparing for a world where tech euphoria no longer drowns out other macro signals, with greater discrimination within the sector.
theme_stances.evidence: October suggests that shield is beginning to crack.

theme_stances.key_argument: Lower oil eases inflation worries and moderates Fed hawkishness to some degree.
theme_stances.evidence: it relieves the inflation worries and arguably moderates Fed hawkishness
